title: Carroll Avenue cottages, DC-line trees, and why added-later metal sweats in the crawl
headline: Carroll Avenue cottages, DC-line trees, and why added-later metal sweats in the crawl
description: Takoma Park, MD bungalows sit on the DC line under a heavy canopy. why later-added ducts collect humidity and leaf grit.

sections.heading: Porch-to-porch lots mean patched dryer vents
paragraphs: Additions sent dryer exhaust through whatever wall was handy. Caps sit in leaf piles. Modern machines push more air than those runs were sized for. Lint packs. Heat and moisture dump back into a bungalow that already has sweating trunks.
If the first AC week smells like a crawl, when you are ready to book, use the [Takoma Park, MD location page](/locations/takoma-park).

sections.heading: Typical signs in a Takoma Park bungalow
listItems: Musty air from a crawl or basement when the AC starts in June.
Leaf-season grit on supplies even after you wipe them.
A dryer that needs two cycles after an addition patched the vent.

sections.heading: Takoma Park walks into three jurisdictions. The humidity does not care.
paragraphs: Old Takoma, Carroll Avenue, and Takoma Junction sit on the Montgomery–Prince George’s–District line. A lot of the housing is early-century bungalows and brick cottages. Ductwork was often added later through crawl spaces and plaster. Those joints were never tight. Maple and oak keep lots shaded and damp.
Older metal runs in a cool crawl sweat through Maryland summers. Pollen and leaf grit stick. The first cool-down in June is when the musty smell shows up at the register.

listItems: Dehumidify crawls in summer even under heavy shade.
Change filters when the canopy is dumping pollen and leaf grit.
Clean ducts every 3 to 5 years; clear patched dryer vents about once a year.
